summary: Count with one-to-one matching, know the last number tells how many, and see up to 5 without counting.
Count out up to 20, count arranged or scattered sets, and name the number after adding one.
Show adding and taking away within 10 in many ways, and connect the different representations.
Solve result-unknown and put-together/take-apart word problems within 10 with objects or drawings.
Recognize and combine small groups with totals up to 5 without counting one by one.
Name squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders and spheres in any size or turn.
Sort the named basic shapes into flat (2D) and solid (3D).
Build and draw triangles, rectangles, squares, hexagons and circles; build cubes, cones, spheres and cylinders.
Solve change-unknown, addend-unknown and compare-difference word problems within 20 with drawings and equations.
Use turn-around and grouping properties as strategies when adding.
Solve unknown-addend problems within 20 by adding on or turning them into subtraction.
Add and subtract within 10 fluently.
Count to 150, starting from any number below 150.
Read and write numerals to 100 and use them to show how many objects.
Identify quarters, dimes and nickels and relate each value to pennies.
Solve one-step word problems within 100 of the harder types, and two-step problems with single digits.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently using mental strategies; knowing all facts from memory is not stated.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently, choosing strategies and explaining why they work.
Add up to three two-digit numbers using place-value strategies and properties.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, yards, centimeters and meters.
Solve word problems with coins up to 99 cents using the cent sign, or whole-dollar amounts using $.
Recognize and draw triangles to hexagons with given attributes; describe attributes of cubes and rectangular prisms.
Explain products of factors up to 10 as equal groups, using arrays, repeated addition and properties.
Explain one-digit divisions as equal groups, using arrays, repeated subtraction or breaking numbers apart.
Solve one-step multiplication and division word problems with numbers up to 10, using arrays, pictures or equations.
Solve unknown-factor problems by dividing or by turning them into multiplication.
Multiply and divide fluently with numbers up to 10, know products from memory, and find unknowns in equations.
Solve two-step word problems with addition, subtraction and multiplication, using an equation with a symbol for the unknown.
Describe multiplication patterns on a hundreds chart or multiplication table.
Add and subtract within 1,000 with estimation, expanded form and the add-subtract relationship.
Use models to multiply a one-digit number by a multiple of 10 from 10 to 90.
Understand unit fractions (halves to eighths) as one equal part of a whole, with area and length models.
Explain what the numerator means in area models and on a number line, for denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, 8.
Show equivalent fractions with area and length models, including fractions equal to one or to whole numbers.
Compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator using models and >, <, =.
Tell time to the minute and solve elapsed-time problems within the same hour.
Measure and estimate length, capacity and weight in customary units, and solve one-step problems with them.
Collect data in up to four categories and show it in frequency tables and scaled picture or bar graphs.
Find a rectangle's area by tiling it with unit squares and counting.
Relate area to multiplying side lengths and to adding the areas of two smaller rectangles.
Find a polygon's perimeter from its sides, or find an unknown side length.
Compose and decompose triangles and quadrilaterals; draw examples and non-examples of quadrilateral types.
Interpret multiplication as comparison and solve times-as-many word problems, telling them apart from additive ones.
Solve two-step whole-number word problems with all operations, estimating and interpreting remainders.
Find all factor pairs of numbers up to 50 and tell multiples, primes and composites.
Explain that each place is ten times the place to its right, up to 100,000.
Read and write whole numbers up to 100,000 in numerals, words and expanded form.
Compare whole numbers up to 100,000 by place value using >, = and <.
Add and subtract whole numbers up to 100,000 with the standard algorithm.
Multiply up to three digits by one digit, and two two-digit numbers, with area models and partial products.
Divide up to three-digit numbers by one-digit numbers with remainders, using models and partial quotients.
Decompose fractions and add or subtract like-denominator fractions and mixed numbers, including word problems.
Multiply a whole number by a fraction (as copies of a unit fraction) and solve related word problems.
Relate tenths and hundredths as fractions and decimals, and add tenths and hundredths.
Measure with metric units (cm, m, g, kg, L, mL) and solve one-step metric word problems.
Convert metric measurements from larger to smaller units using place value and tables.
Solve elapsed-time word problems that cross the hour.
Find areas of rectilinear figures, explore fixed area or perimeter, and use rectangle area and perimeter formulas.
Collect whole-number data and show it in frequency tables, bar graphs or line plots; tell categorical from numerical.
Understand angles in degrees, measure and draw them with a protractor, and find unknown angles.
Classify triangles and quadrilaterals by angles, side lengths, and parallel or perpendicular sides.
Write, explain and evaluate expressions for up to two-step problems, with parentheses and properties.
Explain place-value patterns from millions to thousandths, including multiplying or dividing by powers of ten.
Multiply up to a three-digit number by a two-digit number fluently with the standard algorithm.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit numbers with remainders, using models toward the algorithm.
Solve real-world problems: add, subtract, multiply decimals to thousandths and divide simple decimal cases; estimate.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with related unlike denominators, estimating and solving word problems.
Model fractions as division and solve sharing problems with fraction or mixed-number answers.
Multiply fractions and mixed numbers with models, explain size of products, and solve one-step word problems.
Solve one-step word problems dividing unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
Use a given conversion chart to solve one-step unit conversion problems within one system.
Collect data that change over time and show and read it on a line graph.
Understand volume and measure it by counting unit cubes.
Find rectangular prism volume by packing cubes and by formula, including two joined prisms.
Graph points in the first quadrant and interpret x and y coordinates to solve problems.
Classify quadrilaterals in a hierarchy by their properties.
